male_relative_reproductive_allocation_no.metric: male flower dry biomass divided by vegetative aboveground biomass

limitations: The 2.33× effect is male-flower dry biomass per vegetative biomass, not count of male flowers, viability of pollen, number of mating partners or genetically confirmed selfed offspring
No same-clone repeated genotype across control and male-free treatment; plants from same mixed pool assigned to different environments on average
There are SIX plot-level replicate experimental populations (three each), 272 female plants nested among them and pots; do not treat 272 as independent population replicates
By construction 5% of control plants exceed control-based 95th percentile; incidence direction is non-significant p=.058 even though MRE mean response p=.01
Female reproductive effort difference p=.19 non-significant, which does NOT demonstrate zero cost of opposite-sex male flowers
No male flower pollen viability or source-verified actual offspring selfing rates from this 2021 manipulation
No experiment tested pollen addition independently of male absence, direct sensing cues unverified
2021 original dryad dataset is registered but CSV/text could not be fetched via available tools; no raw individual model refit here
Do not equate 2021 diploid XX female plastic male expression with 2024 hexaploid CMS female retained sterile male flowers, or combine their model coefficients
This plastic response supports preserved developmental ability, not evolutionary restoration of a genetically deleted male function
No allelic rare-type invasion, realized lifetime fitness, SLK Phi/g0/Delta_R, or historical origin directly observed

The all-female treatment doubles the number of females per equal-180-plant population (90 controls vs 180); mate absence is confounded with increased female-neighbour density/competition, and is NOT pure pollen supplementation or direct pollen signal intervention.
